name: application-wallet-connect-button
title: Wallet Connect Button
description: Wallet connection button with three states: disconnected (Connect wallet), connecting (spinner), and connected (status dot, truncated address, and balance).
useWhen: Building a dApp or crypto-adjacent product that authenticates via a blockchain wallet rather than email/OAuth.
You want the connected state to surface the truncated address and balance directly in the trigger, not hidden behind a menu.
Distinct from Social Login Buttons, which authenticate via an OAuth identity provider rather than a wallet address/balance.
avoidWhen: Your app authenticates via email or OAuth only — use Social Login Buttons or Auth Card Shell instead.
You need to support multiple simultaneously connected wallets in one view — this button represents a single active connection.
responsiveBehavior: The connected state's content (address, balance) doesn't wrap; on narrow viewports, hide the balance segment first and keep the truncated address and status dot as the minimum viable connected indicator.
accessibility: Connection status is conveyed by both a colored dot and text/label content, not the dot color alone.
The connecting state uses a real disabled button so it's excluded from the tab order while the action is in flight.
The full (non-truncated) address should be available via a title attribute or accessible description in a full implementation, since the truncated display alone isn't sufficient for verification.

variants.title: Wallet Connect Button
variants.description: Three states: a filled 'Connect wallet' button, a connected state showing a green dot, truncated address, and ETH balance with a menu chevron, and a disabled 'Connecting…' spinner state.
accessibility: The connecting state's spinner button is truly disabled, not just visually dimmed.

variants.title: Wallet Connect Button (Dark)
variants.description: The same three states adapted for dark surfaces.
accessibility: Status dot and text contrast remain legible against the dark surface.
